name: Basic Threat Pattern Repository (K_B)
description: Domain-agnostic phishing indicators used by the Context Enrichment Agent. Formalised in Definition 1 as K_B = {P_c, P_v, P_t}.
common_patterns: Brand logo rendered at high fidelity while the surrounding layout is low fidelity or misaligned.
A single isolated login card on an otherwise empty page with no working site navigation.
Page content mismatched with the hosting domain, or the domain is hidden entirely from the screenshot.
Session-expiry, account-suspension or verification-required framing that demands immediate action.
Multi-brand webmail selector offering Gmail / Yahoo / Outlook / AOL / Office365 tiles on one page.
Generic 'Sign in with your email provider' pages that accept any email domain.
Legal footer, privacy policy and support links present as text but not actually clickable.
Copyright year that is stale or inconsistent with the impersonated brand's live site.
Form submission to an unrelated third-party handler, pastebin or IP-literal endpoint.
CAPTCHA or Cloudflare-style interstitial used as a cloak before the phishing content.
Machine-translated or grammatically inconsistent copy inside an otherwise polished template.
Documents or invoices blurred behind an overlay that requires a login to 'unlock'.
visual_deception: Pixel-level clone of a legitimate brand template, often scraped directly from the real site.
Padlock icons, 'Secure Connection' badges or fake SSL seals drawn into the page body.
Trust badges: Norton Secured, McAfee, VeriSign, BBB, TRUSTe placed near a form.
Fake browser chrome or address bar drawn inside the page to spoof a trusted URL.
Modal overlay dimming a screenshot of the real website behind the credential prompt.
Countdown timers, progress bars or 'remaining attempts' counters manufacturing urgency.
Mobile-app-styled interface used to hide the absence of a real URL bar.
Low-resolution or stretched logo indicating an image lifted from a search result.
Colour scheme and typography copied from the target brand but with wrong spacing or kerning.
Full-screen alert imagery: warning triangles, red banners, sirens, simulated virus scans.
text_manipulation: Urgency: 'act now', 'within 24 hours', 'final notice', 'your account will be closed'.
Fear: 'unusual sign-in detected', 'your device is infected', 'unauthorised transaction'.
Authority: impersonation of IT support, tax authority, police, bank fraud desk, HR.
Reward: prize, refund, cashback, gift card, airdrop or lottery framing.
Scarcity: 'limited slots', 'offer expires today', 'only 3 items left'.
Confidentiality: 'do not share this message', 'verify privately' to discourage checking.
Instructional pressure: 'do not close this window', 'keep the page open until complete'.
Requests for information a legitimate site would never ask for on one screen (password plus OTP plus card plus ID).
url_red_flags: Typosquatting or homoglyph domains: rn for m, 1 for l, Cyrillic lookalikes.
Brand name placed in a subdomain or path rather than the registrable domain.
Free hosting, site builders, or link shorteners standing in for a corporate domain.
Punycode (xn--) domains and long random hyphenated strings.
Raw IP address in the address bar, or non-standard port numbers.
Deeply nested paths that embed the victim's email address as a parameter.
